headline: A 2013 law swaps two Bureau of Land Management offices in a federal permit streamlining pilot project for different offices in Montana and Wyoming.
what_it_does: The law changes a list in the Energy Policy Act of 2005 that names which Bureau of Land Management offices take part in the Federal Permit Streamlining Pilot Project. It removes the Miles City, Montana field office and adds the Montana/Dakotas State Office in Billings. It also removes the Buffalo Field Office in Wyoming and adds the High Plains District Office in Wyoming. The summary does not describe any change in rules, fees, or deadlines.

who_it_affects.group: Energy and mineral developers who apply for federal permits on Bureau of Land Management land in Montana and Wyoming
who_it_affects.how: Their permit applications would be handled by the newly listed offices instead of the ones they replaced, if they take part in the pilot project.

who_it_affects.group: Bureau of Land Management staff at the Miles City and Buffalo field offices
who_it_affects.how: Their offices are no longer named in the pilot project list, which may change how their work on those permits is organized.
